title: IL SB1507: VEH CD-SAFETY ZONES

obligations: A municipality that produces a recorded image of a violation must make the recorded images accessible to the alleged violator by providing a website address accessible through the Internet (Sec. 11-208.8(b))

The automated speed enforcement system shall be operational and violations shall be recorded only at specified times: for school based safety zones, only on school days and no earlier than 6 a.m. and no later than 8:30 p.m. Monday through Thursday, or 9 p.m. on Friday; for park district based safety zones, no earlier than one hour prior to opening and no later than one hour after closing (Sec. 11-208.8(a-5))

For each violation recorded, the municipality having jurisdiction shall issue a written notice of the violation to the registered owner as the alleged violator, delivered by mail within 30 days after the Secretary of State notifies the municipality of the owner's identity, but in no event later than 90 days after the violation (Sec. 11-208.8(e))

The notice must include the name and address of the registered owner, registration number, violation charged, date time and location, a copy of the recorded image or images, amount of civil penalty and payment date, a statement that recorded images are evidence, a warning that failure to pay or contest is an admission of liability, a statement that the person may pay the fine or challenge in court by mail or by administrative hearing, and a website address to view the recorded images (Sec. 11-208.8(f))

The net proceeds that a municipality receives from civil penalties, after deducting all personnel and nonpersonnel costs associated with operation and maintenance, shall be expended or obligated for public safety initiatives around schools and parks, initiatives to improve pedestrian and traffic safety, construction and maintenance of infrastructure including roads and bridges, and after school programs (Sec. 11-208.8(d))

A roadway equipped with an automated speed enforcement system shall be posted with a sign conforming to the national Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices that is visible to approaching traffic stating that vehicle speeds are being photo enforced and indicating the speed limit; the municipality shall install additional signage as it determines necessary to give reasonable notice (Sec. 11-208.8(l))

A roadway where a new automated speed enforcement system is installed shall be posted with signs providing 30 days notice of the use of the new system prior to the issuance of any citations (Sec. 11-208.8(m))

Compensation paid for an automated speed enforcement system must be based on the value of the equipment or services provided and may not be based on the number of traffic citations issued or the revenue generated (Sec. 11-208.8(n))

A municipality using an automated speed enforcement system must provide notice to drivers by publishing the locations of all safety zones where system equipment is installed on the website of the municipality (Sec. 11-208.8(q))

A municipality operating an automated speed enforcement system shall conduct a statistical analysis to assess safety impact after installation and every 2 years thereafter; if operating before the effective date of the amendatory Act of the 103rd General Assembly, by no later than one year after that effective date and every 2 years thereafter; the analysis must be based on best available crash, traffic, and other data, cover before and after installation, be statistically valid, consistent with professional judgment and industry practice, and be made available to the public and published on the municipality website (Sec. 11-208.8(r))

If a county or municipality selects a new vendor and must apply for a permit, approval, or other authorization from the Department for reinstallation of malfunctioning components, and the new vendor operates a system for any other county or municipality in the State, the Department shall approve or deny the application within 90 days after receipt (Sec. 11-208.8(t))

The Department shall adopt rules necessary to implement and administer the revocation process, including describing the revocation process, ensuring notice, and providing an opportunity to appeal (Sec. 11-208.8(u))

The University of Illinois Chicago Urban Transportation Center shall conduct a study including a comprehensive review of City of Chicago website multiyear crash data on North and South DuSable Lake Shore Drive, available research on potential effectiveness of cameras powered by artificial intelligence, analysis of driving behavior, assessment of psychological deterrence, and assessment of how fatalities can be reduced using these cameras and other technical options (Sec. 11-208.8(v))
Upon request of the appropriate authority received within 120 days after the violation, a lessor shall provide within 60 days the name and address of the lessee (Sec. 11-208.8(p))

To demonstrate that the motor vehicle was hijacked or stolen, the owner or lessee must submit proof that a report concerning the motor vehicle or registration plates was filed with a law enforcement agency in a timely manner (Sec. 11-208.8(k))
prohibitions: A penalty may not be imposed if the driver of the motor vehicle received a Uniform Traffic Citation from a police officer for a speeding violation occurring within one eighth of a mile and 15 minutes of the violation recorded by the system (Sec. 11-208.8(c))
No penalty may be imposed if the recorded speed of a vehicle is 5 miles per hour or less over the legal speed limit (Sec. 11-208.8(c))

A violation for which a civil penalty is imposed under this Section is not a violation of a traffic regulation governing the movement of vehicles and may not be recorded on the driving record of the owner (Sec. 11-208.8(c))
Compensation paid for an automated speed enforcement system may not be based on the number of traffic citations issued or the revenue generated by the system (Sec. 11-208.8(n))

No member of the General Assembly and no officer or employee of a municipality or county shall knowingly accept employment or receive compensation or fees for services from a vendor that provides automated speed enforcement system equipment or services to municipalities or counties; no former member of the General Assembly shall within 2 years after termination of service, and no former officer or employee of a municipality or county shall within 2 years after termination of employment, knowingly accept employment or receive compensation or fees from such a vendor (Sec. 11-208.8(n-1))

No person who is the lessor of a motor vehicle pursuant to a written lease agreement shall be liable for an automated speed or traffic law enforcement system violation involving such motor vehicle during the period of the lease, provided the lessor provides the name and address of the lessee within 60 days after a request received within 120 days after the violation (Sec. 11-208.8(p))

Recorded images made by an automated speed enforcement system are confidential and shall be made available only to the alleged violator and governmental and law enforcement agencies for purposes of adjudicating a violation, for statistical purposes, or for other governmental purposes (Sec. 11-208.8(i))

The automated speed enforcement system shall be operational and violations shall be recorded only at the times specified in subsection (a-5), meaning no recording outside those times (Sec. 11-208.8(a-5))
The term safety zone does not include any portion of Lake Shore Drive or any controlled access highway with 8 or more lanes of traffic (Sec. 11-208.8(a))
reading.what_it_does: This Illinois law regulates automated speed enforcement systems in safety zones for municipalities with at least 1,000,000 inhabitants. It defines safety zones around schools and park district recreational facilities, sets when systems may operate, establishes civil penalties for speeding violations recorded by the systems, and imposes notice, signage, data, vendor, and reporting requirements. It also requires a study of artificial intelligence powered cameras on DuSable Lake Shore Drive.
key_definitions: Automated speed enforcement system: a photographic device, radar device, laser device, or other electrical or mechanical device or devices installed or utilized in a safety zone and designed to record the speed of a vehicle and obtain a clear photograph or other recorded image of the vehicle and the vehicle's registration plate or digital registration plate while the driver is violating Article VI of Chapter 11 of this Code or a similar provision of a local ordinance; also a system located in a safety zone under the jurisdiction of a municipality that produces a recorded image of a motor vehicle's violation and is designed to obtain a clear recorded image of the vehicle and license plate, with the recorded image displaying time, date, and location (Sec. 11-208.8(a))
Owner: the person or entity to whom the vehicle is registered (Sec. 11-208.8(a))

Recorded image: images recorded by an automated speed enforcement system on 2 or more photographs, 2 or more microphotographs, 2 or more electronic images, or a video recording showing the motor vehicle and on at least one image or portion of the recording clearly identifying the registration plate or digital registration plate number of the motor vehicle (Sec. 11-208.8(a))

Safety zone: an area within one eighth of a mile from the nearest property line of any public or private elementary or secondary school, or from the nearest property line of any facility, area, or land owned by a school district that is used for educational purposes approved by the Illinois State Board of Education, not including school district headquarters or administrative buildings; also includes an area within one eighth of a mile from the nearest property line of any facility, area, or land owned by a park district used for recreational purposes; if any portion of a roadway is within either one eighth mile radius, the safety zone also includes the roadway extended to the furthest portion of the next furthest intersection; does not include any portion of Lake Shore Drive or any controlled access highway with 8 or more lanes of traffic (Sec. 11-208.8(a))
compliance_steps: Confirm the municipality has a population of 1,000,000 or more and that the proposed location is a safety zone as defined, excluding Lake Shore Drive and controlled access highways with 8 or more lanes (Sec. 11-208.8(a), (s))
Configure the automated speed enforcement system to record violations only during the permitted times for school based or park district based safety zones (Sec. 11-208.8(a-5))

Post required signs conforming to the national Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices and any additional signage; for a new system, post signs providing 30 days notice before issuing citations (Sec. 11-208.8(l), (m))

For each violation, issue a written notice to the registered owner by mail within 30 days after Secretary of State notification and no later than 90 days after the violation, including all required contents (Sec. 11-208.8(e), (f))
Provide the alleged violator with a website address to access the recorded images and keep recorded images confidential except for permitted purposes (Sec. 11-208.8(b), (i))

If selecting a new vendor requiring Department approval, submit the application and expect a decision within 90 days; be aware of Department revocation authority and the 1 year reapplication bar (Sec. 11-208.8(t), (u))

What it does

This Illinois law regulates automated speed enforcement systems in safety zones for municipalities with at least 1,000,000 inhabitants. It defines safety zones around schools and park district recreational facilities, sets when systems may operate, establishes civil penalties for speeding violations recorded by the systems, and imposes notice, signage, data, vendor, and reporting requirements. It also requires a study of artificial intelligence powered cameras on DuSable Lake Shore Drive.

Who it applies to

  • Municipalities with a population of 1,000,000 or more inhabitants (Sec. 11-208.8(s))
  • Registered owners of motor vehicles recorded by an automated speed enforcement system (Sec. 11-208.8(c), (e))
  • Lessors of motor vehicles under written lease agreements (Sec. 11-208.8(p))
  • Vendors providing automated speed enforcement system equipment or services to municipalities or counties (Sec. 11-208.8(n), (n-1))
  • Members of the General Assembly and officers or employees of municipalities or counties (Sec. 11-208.8(n-1))
  • The Department responsible for permits, approvals, or authorizations for automated speed enforcement systems (Sec. 11-208.8(t), (u), (v))
  • The University of Illinois Chicago Urban Transportation Center (Sec. 11-208.8(v))

Effective date

not stated in the text

Key definitions

  • Automated speed enforcement system: a photographic device, radar device, laser device, or other electrical or mechanical device or devices installed or utilized in a safety zone and designed to record the speed of a vehicle and obtain a clear photograph or other recorded image of the vehicle and the vehicle's registration plate or digital registration plate while the driver is violating Article VI of Chapter 11 of this Code or a similar provision of a local ordinance; also a system located in a safety zone under the jurisdiction of a municipality that produces a recorded image of a motor vehicle's violation and is designed to obtain a clear recorded image of the vehicle and license plate, with the recorded image displaying time, date, and location (Sec. 11-208.8(a))
  • Owner: the person or entity to whom the vehicle is registered (Sec. 11-208.8(a))
  • Recorded image: images recorded by an automated speed enforcement system on 2 or more photographs, 2 or more microphotographs, 2 or more electronic images, or a video recording showing the motor vehicle and on at least one image or portion of the recording clearly identifying the registration plate or digital registration plate number of the motor vehicle (Sec. 11-208.8(a))
  • Safety zone: an area within one eighth of a mile from the nearest property line of any public or private elementary or secondary school, or from the nearest property line of any facility, area, or land owned by a school district that is used for educational purposes approved by the Illinois State Board of Education, not including school district headquarters or administrative buildings; also includes an area within one eighth of a mile from the nearest property line of any facility, area, or land owned by a park district used for recreational purposes; if any portion of a roadway is within either one eighth mile radius, the safety zone also includes the roadway extended to the furthest portion of the next furthest intersection; does not include any portion of Lake Shore Drive or any controlled access highway with 8 or more lanes of traffic (Sec. 11-208.8(a))

Obligations

  • A municipality that produces a recorded image of a violation must make the recorded images accessible to the alleged violator by providing a website address accessible through the Internet (Sec. 11-208.8(b))
  • The automated speed enforcement system shall be operational and violations shall be recorded only at specified times: for school based safety zones, only on school days and no earlier than 6 a.m. and no later than 8:30 p.m. Monday through Thursday, or 9 p.m. on Friday; for park district based safety zones, no earlier than one hour prior to opening and no later than one hour after closing (Sec. 11-208.8(a-5))
  • For each violation recorded, the municipality having jurisdiction shall issue a written notice of the violation to the registered owner as the alleged violator, delivered by mail within 30 days after the Secretary of State notifies the municipality of the owner's identity, but in no event later than 90 days after the violation (Sec. 11-208.8(e))
  • The notice must include the name and address of the registered owner, registration number, violation charged, date time and location, a copy of the recorded image or images, amount of civil penalty and payment date, a statement that recorded images are evidence, a warning that failure to pay or contest is an admission of liability, a statement that the person may pay the fine or challenge in court by mail or by administrative hearing, and a website address to view the recorded images (Sec. 11-208.8(f))
  • The net proceeds that a municipality receives from civil penalties, after deducting all personnel and nonpersonnel costs associated with operation and maintenance, shall be expended or obligated for public safety initiatives around schools and parks, initiatives to improve pedestrian and traffic safety, construction and maintenance of infrastructure including roads and bridges, and after school programs (Sec. 11-208.8(d))
  • A roadway equipped with an automated speed enforcement system shall be posted with a sign conforming to the national Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices that is visible to approaching traffic stating that vehicle speeds are being photo enforced and indicating the speed limit; the municipality shall install additional signage as it determines necessary to give reasonable notice (Sec. 11-208.8(l))
  • A roadway where a new automated speed enforcement system is installed shall be posted with signs providing 30 days notice of the use of the new system prior to the issuance of any citations (Sec. 11-208.8(m))
  • Compensation paid for an automated speed enforcement system must be based on the value of the equipment or services provided and may not be based on the number of traffic citations issued or the revenue generated (Sec. 11-208.8(n))
  • A municipality using an automated speed enforcement system must provide notice to drivers by publishing the locations of all safety zones where system equipment is installed on the website of the municipality (Sec. 11-208.8(q))
  • A municipality operating an automated speed enforcement system shall conduct a statistical analysis to assess safety impact after installation and every 2 years thereafter; if operating before the effective date of the amendatory Act of the 103rd General Assembly, by no later than one year after that effective date and every 2 years thereafter; the analysis must be based on best available crash, traffic, and other data, cover before and after installation, be statistically valid, consistent with professional judgment and industry practice, and be made available to the public and published on the municipality website (Sec. 11-208.8(r))
  • If a county or municipality selects a new vendor and must apply for a permit, approval, or other authorization from the Department for reinstallation of malfunctioning components, and the new vendor operates a system for any other county or municipality in the State, the Department shall approve or deny the application within 90 days after receipt (Sec. 11-208.8(t))
  • The Department shall adopt rules necessary to implement and administer the revocation process, including describing the revocation process, ensuring notice, and providing an opportunity to appeal (Sec. 11-208.8(u))
  • The University of Illinois Chicago Urban Transportation Center shall conduct a study including a comprehensive review of City of Chicago website multiyear crash data on North and South DuSable Lake Shore Drive, available research on potential effectiveness of cameras powered by artificial intelligence, analysis of driving behavior, assessment of psychological deterrence, and assessment of how fatalities can be reduced using these cameras and other technical options (Sec. 11-208.8(v))
  • Upon request of the appropriate authority received within 120 days after the violation, a lessor shall provide within 60 days the name and address of the lessee (Sec. 11-208.8(p))
  • To demonstrate that the motor vehicle was hijacked or stolen, the owner or lessee must submit proof that a report concerning the motor vehicle or registration plates was filed with a law enforcement agency in a timely manner (Sec. 11-208.8(k))

Prohibitions

  • A penalty may not be imposed if the driver of the motor vehicle received a Uniform Traffic Citation from a police officer for a speeding violation occurring within one eighth of a mile and 15 minutes of the violation recorded by the system (Sec. 11-208.8(c))
  • No penalty may be imposed if the recorded speed of a vehicle is 5 miles per hour or less over the legal speed limit (Sec. 11-208.8(c))
  • A violation for which a civil penalty is imposed under this Section is not a violation of a traffic regulation governing the movement of vehicles and may not be recorded on the driving record of the owner (Sec. 11-208.8(c))
  • Compensation paid for an automated speed enforcement system may not be based on the number of traffic citations issued or the revenue generated by the system (Sec. 11-208.8(n))
  • No member of the General Assembly and no officer or employee of a municipality or county shall knowingly accept employment or receive compensation or fees for services from a vendor that provides automated speed enforcement system equipment or services to municipalities or counties; no former member of the General Assembly shall within 2 years after termination of service, and no former officer or employee of a municipality or county shall within 2 years after termination of employment, knowingly accept employment or receive compensation or fees from such a vendor (Sec. 11-208.8(n-1))
  • No person who is the lessor of a motor vehicle pursuant to a written lease agreement shall be liable for an automated speed or traffic law enforcement system violation involving such motor vehicle during the period of the lease, provided the lessor provides the name and address of the lessee within 60 days after a request received within 120 days after the violation (Sec. 11-208.8(p))
  • Recorded images made by an automated speed enforcement system are confidential and shall be made available only to the alleged violator and governmental and law enforcement agencies for purposes of adjudicating a violation, for statistical purposes, or for other governmental purposes (Sec. 11-208.8(i))
  • The automated speed enforcement system shall be operational and violations shall be recorded only at the times specified in subsection (a-5), meaning no recording outside those times (Sec. 11-208.8(a-5))
  • The term safety zone does not include any portion of Lake Shore Drive or any controlled access highway with 8 or more lanes of traffic (Sec. 11-208.8(a))

Penalties and enforcement

Civil penalties are imposed on the owner of a motor vehicle used in a traffic violation recorded by an automated speed enforcement system: if recorded speed is 6 to 10 miles per hour over the legal limit, a civil penalty not exceeding $50, plus an additional penalty of not more than $50 for failure to pay timely; if recorded speed is more than 10 miles per hour over, a civil penalty not exceeding $100, plus an additional penalty of not more than $100 for failure to pay timely (Sec. 11-208.8(c)). A penalty may not be imposed if the driver received a Uniform Traffic Citation within one eighth of a mile and 15 minutes of the recorded violation, or if the recorded speed is 5 miles per hour or less over the limit (Sec. 11-208.8(c)). The municipality issues the written notice and may send a speed violation warning notice for speeds 5 miles per hour or less over the limit (Sec. 11-208.8(c), (e)). A notice alleging the violation is evidence of the facts and admissible in any proceeding (Sec. 11-208.8(h)). Recorded images may be admissible in any proceeding resulting from the citation (Sec. 11-208.8(i)). The court or hearing officer may consider defenses including stolen vehicle or plates, hijacking, driver received a Uniform Traffic Citation, and any other evidence or issues provided by municipal ordinance (Sec. 11-208.8(j)). To demonstrate theft or hijacking, the owner or lessee must submit proof of a timely report to a law enforcement agency (Sec. 11-208.8(k)). The Department may revoke any permit, approval, or other authorization if an official or employee is charged with bribery, official misconduct, or a similar crime related to the system; the Department adopts rules for revocation, notice, and appeal, and a revoked municipality or county may not reapply for 1 year (Sec. 11-208.8(u)). The statute does not state a private right of action.

How it affects AI deployment

  • The law does not directly authorize or prohibit the deployment of artificial intelligence powered cameras for speed enforcement; it requires the University of Illinois Chicago Urban Transportation Center to conduct a study of such cameras on North and South DuSable Lake Shore Drive, including their potential effectiveness, driving behavior analysis, psychological deterrence, and alternatives (Sec. 11-208.8(v)).
  • An organisation deploying automated speed enforcement systems, including any system that uses artificial intelligence as an electrical or mechanical device to record speed and images, must comply with the operational time limits, signage, notice, confidentiality, vendor compensation, and statistical analysis requirements if the system is in a safety zone within a municipality of 1,000,000 or more inhabitants (Sec. 11-208.8(a), (a-5), (b), (e), (f), (i), (l), (m), (n), (q), (r), (s)).
  • The Department may revoke permits for automated speed enforcement systems if an official or employee is charged with bribery, official misconduct, or a similar crime related to the system, which could affect an organisation operating such a system (Sec. 11-208.8(u)).

Notable exemptions

  • Safety zone does not include Lake Shore Drive or any controlled access highway with 8 or more lanes of traffic (Sec. 11-208.8(a))
  • No penalty may be imposed if the recorded speed is 5 miles per hour or less over the legal speed limit (Sec. 11-208.8(c))
  • No penalty may be imposed if the driver received a Uniform Traffic Citation from a police officer for a speeding violation occurring within one eighth of a mile and 15 minutes of the recorded violation (Sec. 11-208.8(c))
  • A violation for which a civil penalty is imposed is not recorded on the driving record of the owner (Sec. 11-208.8(c))
  • A lessor under a written lease agreement is not liable for a violation during the lease period if the lessor provides the lessee's name and address within 60 days after a request received within 120 days after the violation (Sec. 11-208.8(p))
  • This Section applies only to municipalities with a population of 1,000,000 or more inhabitants (Sec. 11-208.8(s))
  • Recorded images are confidential and available only to the alleged violator and governmental and law enforcement agencies for limited purposes (Sec. 11-208.8(i))

Compliance steps

  • Confirm the municipality has a population of 1,000,000 or more and that the proposed location is a safety zone as defined, excluding Lake Shore Drive and controlled access highways with 8 or more lanes (Sec. 11-208.8(a), (s))
  • Configure the automated speed enforcement system to record violations only during the permitted times for school based or park district based safety zones (Sec. 11-208.8(a-5))
  • Post required signs conforming to the national Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices and any additional signage; for a new system, post signs providing 30 days notice before issuing citations (Sec. 11-208.8(l), (m))
  • Ensure vendor compensation is based on equipment or services value, not citations or revenue, and comply with employment restrictions for General Assembly members and municipal or county officers and employees (Sec. 11-208.8(n), (n-1))
  • Publish the locations of all safety zones where system equipment is installed on the municipality website (Sec. 11-208.8(q))
  • For each violation, issue a written notice to the registered owner by mail within 30 days after Secretary of State notification and no later than 90 days after the violation, including all required contents (Sec. 11-208.8(e), (f))
  • Provide the alleged violator with a website address to access the recorded images and keep recorded images confidential except for permitted purposes (Sec. 11-208.8(b), (i))
  • If a lessor provides lessee information, issue the violation to the lessee in the same manner as to a registered owner (Sec. 11-208.8(p))
  • Conduct and publish a statistical analysis of safety impact after installation and every 2 years thereafter, or by the required deadline if operating before the effective date of the amendatory Act of the 103rd General Assembly (Sec. 11-208.8(r))
  • If selecting a new vendor requiring Department approval, submit the application and expect a decision within 90 days; be aware of Department revocation authority and the 1 year reapplication bar (Sec. 11-208.8(t), (u))
  • If the system uses artificial intelligence powered cameras on DuSable Lake Shore Drive, note that the law requires a study by the University of Illinois Chicago Urban Transportation Center, not immediate deployment authority (Sec. 11-208.8(v))
